claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-014 was policy-compliant because the admissible due-diligence record showed a material unresolved control risk at decision time.
specific_concerns: The cited record, as summarized, shows a quality-process gap, an inconsistency in storage-control materials, and a recommendation for follow-up before approval, but the policy states those facts justify follow-up or escalation and do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
No admissible evidence is identified showing that the unresolved issues were formally assessed as material enough to require rejection rather than further diligence or escalation.
The actor's packet itself characterizes support for rejection as limited/weak, which is below the policy threshold for a clean rejection decision.
Because evidence access is limited to the actor summary only, there is no independent basis to verify whether any formally logged material security finding exists.
unsupported_claims: The claim that the admissible record supports rejection, rather than follow-up or escalation, is not adequately supported on the summarized evidence provided.
The claim that approval was not adequately supported at decision time because diligence issues remained unresolved does not, on its own, satisfy the stated policy threshold for vendor rejection.
Any implied reject-level control failure is unsupported absent a formally logged material risk determination.
evidence_requests: Provide any formally logged due-diligence record explicitly concluding that the control issue was material and unresolved at the time of decision.
Provide the governing procurement decision rule or escalation matrix showing that the documented facts require rejection rather than conditional follow-up or escalation.
Provide the full admissible text or excerpts for BPROC-014-C, BPROC-014-D, and BPROC-014-E so materiality and timing can be independently assessed.
Confirm whether any private security-review result influenced the rejection and, if so, whether it was formally logged and admissible.
decision_criteria: Reject only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies alone support follow-up or escalation, not automatic rejection.
Do not rely on private security-review results unless they were formally logged.
Require a support link from the cited evidence to the actual reject-level policy predicate, not merely to general diligence incompleteness.
